title: Fix metrics cardinality for failover_reason/trigger_source labels
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: - Failover decision metrics now use bounded enums for failover_reason/trigger_source and drop high-cardinality labels (tenant_id, route_id). - Adds safeguards + telemetry for rejected/unknown label values to prevent silent cardinality regressions.
description:
Title: Fix metrics cardinality for failover_reason/trigger_source labels

Context
During staging rehearsals for Regional Failover Automation (ENG-2418) we saw a sharp increase in time series for failover decision metrics. Root cause: we were emitting raw, free-form strings into failover_reason and trigger_source (e.g., concatenated signal names / error messages), and we also carried request- or policy-specific identifiers as labels in a few code paths. This becomes particularly painful during noisy/partial impairments where the controller evaluates frequently and produces many distinct label values.

This PR reduces label cardinality by (1) mapping reasons/sources to bounded enums, (2) removing high-cardinality labels from the exported series, and (3) adding guardrails that reject unexpected values and surface them via dedicated counters + structured logs.

What changed
- Bounded enums
  - Introduced FailoverReason enum: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | operator | config_change | unknown
  - Introduced TriggerSource enum: region_health | perf_canary | gateway | controller | operator_cli | unknown
  - All call sites now translate internal signal identifiers to these enums via a single mapping table.
  - Unknown/unmapped inputs are coerced to "unknown" (not the raw string).

- Label set cleanup (cardinality reduction)
  - Removed labels: tenant_id, route_id, policy_id, model_id from exported metrics.
  - Kept bounded labels that are useful for SLO slicing without exploding series: environment, scope (hosted|dedicated), from_region, to_region, tenant_tier (free|pro|enterprise), action (recommend|execute|rollback).

- Aggregation safeguards
  - Added rw_failover_metric_label_reject_total{metric, label, scope} counter that increments when a value is rejected/coerced.
  - Added a small in-process LRU to rate-limit log spam for unknown label values (logs include the original value + call-site tag).
  - Added unit tests that fail if a new FailoverReason/TriggerSource is introduced without updating the mapping table.

- Backwards compatibility / rollout
  - The old metrics names remain, but their label sets are changed (same series name, fewer labels).
  - Dashboards/alerts PR will follow in observability-pack; this PR includes inline comments pointing to the new label names.
  - NOTE: anyone doing ad-hoc queries that group by tenant_id/route_id will need to switch to logs/audit events (see pr-19824-failover-event-audit-log).

Metric details
- rw_failover_decision_total{scope, action, failover_reason, trigger_source, from_region, to_region, tenant_tier, environment}
- rw_failover_metric_label_reject_total{metric, label, scope, environment}

Why this is safe
- The controller/auditing behavior is unchanged; this is strictly telemetry shaping.
- Unknown values are not dropped silently; they are coerced to "unknown" and we emit a reject counter + structured logs.

Testing
- Unit: metrics mapping + label guard tests (added).
- Integration: exercised controller decision loop in staging (dry-run) and verified series counts in Prometheus stayed flat under noisy signals.

Follow-ups
- Update dashboards/alerts to use new label set (tracked under ENG-2418 and handled in observability-pack).
- After game day, re-check rw_failover_metric_label_reject_total for unexpected spikes (indicates missing mapping or new signal names).

Links
- Related: pr-19816-add-multi-region-slo-metrics, pr-19818-alerts-failover-burn-rate, pr-19824-failover-event-audit-log
- Notes: engineering/observability/failover-metrics-cardinality-review

review_conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Can we guarantee failover_reason/trigger_source are truly bounded (no accidental passthrough)? Also, removing tenant_id/route_id will break a couple internal Grafana panels—are we coordinating updates? 

Sergio Costa (author): Yep—mapping is centralized in signal_mapping.go and unknowns are coerced to "unknown" with a reject counter. I’ll open a follow-up in observability-pack to update dashboards/alerts; I added comments in docs/ops/metrics/failover-metrics.md with example queries.

Miles Thornton (review): +1 on coercing unknowns. Please add a test that fails when a new internal signal name is introduced without mapping. 

Sergio Costa (author): Added mapping coverage tests for both controller and policy engine call sites.

Benji Okafor (review): Any chance we still emit policy_id somewhere through tags? We’ve had this happen via helper wrappers. 

Sergio Costa (author): Good catch—there was one wrapper path in eval_metrics.go; removed and added a guard that rejects label keys outside the allowlist.

Aisha Bello (approval): Looks good. The reject counter is exactly what we need for early warning. Approved after the test addition.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Please post in #eng-sre once merged so on-call knows to update ad-hoc queries.
